Example catalogue

This catalogue covers 67 tracked programs, including 46 mathematics programs. It documents source behavior and authored test registrations; it records no new execution results.

The mathematics guide gives each mathematical program’s algorithm, domain, arithmetic, checks and limits. The Navier–Stokes guide and AI mathematics guide retain their explanatory narratives and references.

The general examples runner discovers 66 flat programs and compiles/runs them with native AOT. 4 require ESHKOL_QUANTUM_ENABLED=ON; 0 current paths match the existing proprietary/unreleased exclusion patterns. The 1 nested artifact generator is outside that glob. Discovery and a successful process are distinct from an asserted mathematical verdict.

The NS/IPM CMake lists declare native JIT/AOT tests under ESHKOL_BUILD_TESTS AND TARGET eshkol-run; this matrix does not claim that any particular build configured, ran or passed them, or that every example is supported by the bytecode VM.

For manual AOT commands below, create .scratch/example-manual once from the repository root.

To check documentation drift: python3 scripts/build_example_catalogue.py --check. After deliberate source/semantic review, update the catalogue and run --write; the generator never updates fingerprints or executes examples.

Language and application examples

These descriptions report implemented checks or printed diagnostics; output prose is not treated as an assertion.

Scalar automatic differentiation

Source: autodiff.esk. SHA-256: 37bf8a530c57f041f1badb49cc8aeadf1decf23f0c72a2323034709540222e1f.

Purpose: Introduce derivative and gradient calls on simple scalar polynomials.

Implemented algorithm: Differentiate x³ and x³+2x; create a reusable derivative closure.

Domain and parameters: x=2,3,5; expected displayed derivatives 12,29,75.

Arithmetic: Floating-point scalar inputs.

Checks in the source: Prints results and expected comments; it contains no pass/fail assertion.

Limits: An introductory output demonstration, not a convergence or performance benchmark.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

Implementation/check anchors: line 1, line 5, line 6, line 7, line 13, line 18.

Manual commands from the repository root, after satisfying the prerequisites:

./build/eshkol-run -r examples/autodiff.esk
./build/eshkol-run -L./build examples/autodiff.esk -o .scratch/example-manual/autodiff && .scratch/example-manual/autodiff

Projectile launch-angle fitting

Source: differentiable_physics.esk. SHA-256: e0ca3c23bba825102d5fc1ba8311e698701728baf3b325864c9799ca4dd7e33f.

Purpose: Differentiate a recursive numerical trajectory to fit landing distance.

Implemented algorithm: Euler-step linear-drag dynamics and apply gradient descent to squared horizontal landing error.

Domain and parameters: g=9.81,k=0.08,v₀=14,target=12; dt=0.01,max 800 steps; θ₀=0.5,lr=0.00005,200 updates.

Arithmetic: Floating-point integration and AD.

Checks in the source: Prints initial/final angle, landing distance and error; no convergence threshold assertion.

Limits: Discrete landing termination and a fixed time step limit the model; no global optimizer, continuum accuracy bound or measured speed claim.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

H₂ harmonic frequency from Taylor AD

Source: h2_vibrational.esk. SHA-256: 5d43fbd0b72dd49dc125794b697ec79b3d5bd958a9084630653ab498d29191b3.

Purpose: Compute molecular curvature through the source’s Gaussian-integral energy model.

Implemented algorithm: Implement Boys/erf approximations, STO-3G integrals and a 2×2 full-CI eigenvalue; find an equilibrium and take derivative-n order two.

Domain and parameters: Fixed STO-3G hydrogen exponents/coefficients and reduced mass 1836.15267343/2; source-defined equilibrium iteration.

Arithmetic: Floating-point molecular model and analytic AD through its implemented approximations.

Checks in the source: Prints equilibrium, energy, curvature and cm⁻¹ conversion; no experimental-agreement assertion.

Limits: “Exact derivative” refers to differentiating this code without finite differences, not exact-real arithmetic or basis-complete/experimental molecular accuracy.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

H₂ geometry AD and quantum response

Source: h2_vibrational_full.esk. SHA-256: 3be1fcc934fc79cec88c4530de4a8c8a7506b22046e23e75ef137d5053e66a92.

Purpose: Combine Pauli-coefficient geometry derivatives with quantum-state response.

Implemented algorithm: Differentiate g_i(R), evaluate H/H′/H″ through Moonlab, estimate the parameter Hessian by finite differences of gradients and solve a 4×4 response system.

Domain and parameters: Two-qubit H₂ Pauli basis II,IZ,ZI,ZZ,XX; source-selected equilibrium/ansatz; Hessian ε=1e-4.

Arithmetic: Floating-point Taylor AD, backend quantum quantities and a finite-difference parameter Hessian.

Checks in the source: Prints frozen term, response, force constant and frequency; no assertion verifies agreement or response magnitude.

Limits: The parameter Hessian is not wholly AD-derived; model/backend and finite-difference approximation remain explicit.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run/stdlib, agent.quantum and the existing Moonlab quantum backend; the general examples suite requires ESHKOL_QUANTUM_ENABLED=ON for this file.

H₂ frequency from quantum-backend geometry differences

Source: h2_vibrational_quantum.esk. SHA-256: 1afb2473ed1a79d281d24c71e0a3f429f6411cf86bdcf9cd8dd971b49f9474e5.

Purpose: Compute curvature of the backend energy surface by three-point differencing.

Implemented algorithm: Evaluate exact-ground-energy backend calls at three bond lengths and convert the central second difference to a frequency.

Domain and parameters: R₀=0.740 Å,step=0.02 Å; energies at 0.72,0.74,0.76 Å; fixed mass/bohr conversion.

Arithmetic: Floating-point backend energies and finite differences.

Checks in the source: Prints energies, curvature and frequency; a displayed agreement claim is not an executable comparison with h2_vibrational.esk.

Limits: Accuracy depends on energy-surface smoothness and step size; no independent exact derivative or experimental validation is asserted.

Prerequisites: Built eshkol-run/stdlib, agent.quantum and the existing Moonlab quantum backend; the general examples suite requires ESHKOL_QUANTUM_ENABLED=ON for this file.

Domain and parameters: a=2 Pa,b=3,e₀=0,|t|≤0.2; source emits a maximum of 4096 samples and generation/status fields.
